findings.title: SQL injection in the order lookup lets any visitor read the whole database

severity.label: critical
severity.reasoning: Reachable over the network with no login, and it exposes and can alter every table the application account can reach.

flaw.description: The order id from the URL is formatted straight into a SQL string. Nothing between the route and the query parses or binds it, so the caller controls the statement.

flow.quote: sql = f"SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = {order_id}"

steps: Request /orders?id=1 to confirm the endpoint answers.
Request /orders?id=1 UNION SELECT email, password_hash, 3, 4 FROM users.
Read every user's email and password hash from the response body.
chains_into: Offline cracking of the unsalted hashes, then account takeover.

proof.summary: The script sends the UNION payload and checks that a seeded user's email comes back.
proof.result:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
[{"id": "alice@example.test", "total": "5f4dcc3b5aa765d61d8327deb882cf99"}]
POC OK: leaked 1 seeded credential row
proof.isolation: container, no network egress, read-only root, 512 MiB, 60 s

gains: Read access to every table the application account can read.
blast_radius.kill_chain: Unauthenticated request, then database read, then credential cracking, then login as any user.

remediation.summary: Bind the order id as a query parameter and reject non-numeric ids at the route.
remediation.patch:
--- a/app/routes/orders.py
+++ b/app/routes/orders.py
@@ -40,5 +40,5 @@
     order_id = request.args.get("id")
-    sql = f"SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = {order_id}"
-    rows = db.run(sql)
+    rows = db.run("SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = ?", (int(order_id),))
     return jsonify(rows)
remediation.why: A bound parameter is sent as data, so the database never parses it as SQL.
defense_in_depth: Give the application a database account that cannot read the users table.
Hash passwords with a slow, salted algorithm.

confidence.reason: The proof of concept ran in the sandbox and returned a seeded credential row.

findings.title: Reflected cross-site scripting in the search page

severity.label: high
severity.reasoning: Needs a logged-in victim's session to be worth anything, and then reads what that session can read.

flaw.description: The q parameter is echoed into the results heading without encoding.

flow.note: Marker sent in the query string.
Marker reflected with the tag intact.

preconditions: The victim is logged in and follows a link the attacker supplies.
steps: Send the victim a link to /search with a script payload in q.
The payload runs in the victim's session.

proof.summary: A harmless marker with angle brackets was reflected unencoded.
proof.reason: The scope file allows passive checks only, so no script payload was sent.

gains: Actions and reads as the victim.

remediation.summary: HTML-encode q where the template writes it, and send a Content-Security-Policy that forbids inline script.

confidence.reason: The reflection was observed in a live response; script execution was not tested.

findings.title: The application container runs as root

severity.label: medium
severity.reasoning: Label carried over from the scanner rule; it matters only after another flaw gives code execution.

flaw.description: The Dockerfile never sets USER, so the process runs as uid 0 inside the container.

proof.reason: A configuration weakness with no direct trigger; there is nothing to run.

remediation.summary: Create an unprivileged user in the image and switch to it with USER.

confidence.reason: Reported by one scanner rule and not checked against the deployed runtime settings.

findings.title: Password reset tokens are derived with MD5

severity.label: low
severity.reasoning: Needs local access and a privileged position to observe tokens.

flaw.description: Reset tokens are the MD5 of the user id and a timestamp, which is guessable.

proof.reason: The token recipe is visible in the code; no token was forged.

remediation.summary: Generate reset tokens from the operating system's random source.
remediation.patch:
--- a/app/auth/tokens.py
+++ b/app/auth/tokens.py
@@ -17,3 +17,1 @@
-    raw = f"{user.id}{time.time()}"
-    return hashlib.md5(raw.encode()).hexdigest()
+    return secrets.token_urlsafe(32)

confidence.reason: Traced from the reset handler to the token function.

dismissed.title: Path traversal in the file download handler

severity.label: medium
severity.reasoning: Would expose files readable by the application.

flaw.description: The name parameter is joined onto the upload directory.

confidence.reason: The join looked unsafe before the caller was read.

dismissed.dismiss_reason: The caller passes the name through secure_filename two lines earlier, so no separator reaches the join.
